prerequisites: Having acquired the competencies corresponding to the subjects of previous semesters.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems.
Capacity for autonomous and deep learning.

Be able to explain and apply understandably the phenomena and processes that occur in electrical circuits and elementary electrical machines using the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines, using appropriate magnitudes and units.
Ability to analytically analyze electrical circuits.
Ability to solve exercises of elementary electrical machines.
Be able to record experimental data in practical electrical circuits and have the ability to analyze them.
Be able to analyze electrical circuits using computer simulation techniques.

syllabus_topics: 2.3. Complex representation of a sinusoidal magnitude
2.4. Derivative and integral of a sinusoidal magnitude
2.5. The time domain and the frequency domain
3.1. Circuit analysis by the mesh method
3.2. Circuit analysis by the node method
3.5. Maximum power transfer theorem in direct current
4. Power in sinusoidal alternating current circuits
4.1. Power in sinusoidal alternating current regime
4.5. Maximum power transfer theorem in alternating current
P.2 DC laboratory instrumentation. The multimeter and the power supply
P.3 Kirchhoff's Laws in a DC circuit
P.4 AC laboratory instrumentation. The function generator and the oscilloscope
P.6 RLC circuit in AC. Impedance
P.8 Three-phase systems (I). Power factor compensation
P.9 Three-phase systems (II). Power factor compensation
teaching_methods: Individual and autonomous study and work, including individual study and autonomous work by the student for the assimilation of theoretical and practical contents, as well as group work for the preparation of laboratory practice reports.
Tutorials, personalized attention to students, including academic tutorials through the virtual campus.
Written exam that evaluates the student's ability to solve problems related to the theoretical contents of the subject.
Continuous evaluation of performance in the laboratory, including the execution of experimental setups and their simulations, as well as answering test-type questionnaires on their contents.
Lectures, where the professor will explain the theoretical contents of the subject's program, interspersed with practical examples to facilitate understanding.
Problem-solving classes, where exercises and problems are proposed, discussed, and solved, applying the theoretical concepts explained in theory classes.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices (continuous performance evaluation, experimental setups, simulations, test-type questionnaires)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on an 80% weight for the theory exam and a 20% weight for continuous evaluation of laboratory practices. Attendance at laboratory practice classes is mandatory. The theory exam is a written test solving problems related to the course content. Laboratory practice evaluation includes experimental setups, simulations, and test-type questionnaires.
